newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam floods affecting nearly two million.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam floods affecting nearly two million.

text.p: Flooding in southern Vietnam's Mekong Delta has claimed 27 lives, most of them children, and is now affecting more than 1.8 million people, relief agencies said on Wednesday.
Officials with the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said floodwaters in provinces across the region were continuing to rise.
They said all but three of the deaths so far were children and put the total number of people affected at 1,813,151, more than 77,000 of whom had been evacuated from their homes.
Flooding in the lower stretches of the Mekong River is an annual threat, often claiming scores of lives in one of the most densely populated regions of the country and in neighbouring Cambodia.
But Vietnam's domestic media reported on Wednesday that this season's water levels were approaching their highest in nearly 20 years.
IFRC officials said they expected the peak of the flooding in a week's time. They said 227,706 homes were already submerged and some three thousand km (2,000 miles) of dikes broken.
Damage to crops in the area, the country's southern rice-bowl, was relatively minor thanks to early harvesting.
The English-language Vietnam News reported on Wednesday that Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet had instructed local authorities and agencies to step up efforts to help people affected.
